short_en: Not on its own. Feelings are a gift, but they change like the weather. Faith stands on solid ground: good reasons, God's word, and the witness of the Church. Feel Him close? Thank Him. Feel nothing? He is still there.
short_ar: ليس وحده. المشاعر عطيّة جميلة، لكنها تتبدّل كالطقس. الإيمان يقف على أرض صلبة: أسباب معقولة، وكلمة الله، وشهادة الكنيسة. تشعر بقربه؟ اشكره. لا تشعر بشيء؟ هو باقٍ هناك.
share_en: Feelings are the weather. Faith is the ground under your feet.
share_ar: المشاعر طقسٌ يتبدّل، أمّا الإيمان فالأرض الثابتة تحت قدميك.
anim: A house stands on a rock while the sky above it keeps changing (sun, clouds, storm, sun); the sky is labelled "feelings," the rock "reasons + God's word," and the house never moves.

en.story:
C.S. Lewis lost his faith as a teenager and became an atheist Oxford scholar. In 1929 he finally admitted that God was God, but he felt no joy at all. He called himself "the most dejected and reluctant convert in all England." His feelings said no; his reasoning, and long talks with friends like J.R.R. Tolkien, said yes. In 1931 he became a Christian, and later wrote Mere Christianity. His faith did not begin with a feeling. (Notre Dame Ethics Center, Religion Unplugged)

Honest note: Lewis became an Anglican, not a Catholic. We can learn much from him, but he is not our guide on what divides Catholics and Anglicans.
en.deeper: The course names two kinds of evidence. Objective evidence anyone can check: arguments, history, science. Subjective evidence is personal, like sensing God in prayer, and it can give real knowledge: someone can know God this way before hearing any argument (SoA God L1, p. 10). But a feeling is hard to share and easy to doubt. Critics even say our brains are wired to imagine invisible agents. The course answers: a brain mechanism does not settle whether God is real; God may have given us that instinct so we would seek Him (SoA God L3, pp. 15–16). The Church adds that strong feelings do not measure holiness (CCC 1768), and that times of dryness in prayer are a moment to cling to Jesus by faith (CCC 2731). Lewis called faith holding on to what reason has accepted, whatever our moods.
en.proof: • In 2006, University of Montreal researchers scanned the brains of 15 Carmelite nuns as they relived their deepest moment with God. Many brain regions became active, not one "God spot." (Nature News, 2006) A scan shows that a feeling happens in the brain. It cannot show whether God is its source, just as a scan of a child seeing his mother cannot tell you if the mother is real.

en.talk: Have you ever felt very close to God, then felt nothing? What kept you going, or what could?
